_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Burkina Faso covering Mossi Kingdoms, French Upper Volta, Sankara revolution, and contemporary jihadist crisis.

ethnic_groups.name: Mossi
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant ethnic group; centralised kingdoms (Ouagadougou, Yatenga, Tenkodogo); Mogho Naba paramount chief; Mooré language

ethnic_groups.name: Fulani/Peul
ethnic_groups.notes: Pastoralists across the Sahel zone; Fulfulde language; caught between jihadist recruitment and state suspicion

ethnic_groups.name: Bobo
ethnic_groups.notes: Western Burkina Faso around Bobo-Dioulasso; farming people; traditional festivals

ethnic_groups.name: Gurunsi
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border with Ghana; includes Kassena, Nankana, and Lela subgroups; distinctive painted houses

ethnic_groups.name: Gurma/Gourmantché
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Burkina; related to kingdom of Fada N'Gourma

ethnic_groups.name: Senufo
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern region; related to Senufo in Côte d'Ivoire and Mali

ethnic_groups.name: Lobi
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern Burkina; acephalous society; earth-shrine governance; distinctive terracotta sculpture

ethnic_groups.name: Mande/Dioula
ethnic_groups.notes: Trading communities, especially in Bobo-Dioulasso; linked to West African Mande diaspora

ethnic_groups.name: Tuareg
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Sahel; nomadic Berber pastoralists; Tamashek language

ethnic_groups.name: Dagara
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern Burkina; farming people straddling Ghana border

independence.notes: As Upper Volta; renamed Burkina Faso 1984

natural_resources.notes: Africa's fastest-growing gold producer (4th in Africa); artisanal mining (orpaillage) employs ~1M; cotton 'white gold' second export; manganese reserves significant; no oil/gas
natural_resources.resource_curse_risk: Moderate (gold mining revenue allocation; artisanal mining unregulated)

military.notes: Two coups in 2022 (Damiba Jan, Traoré Sep); junta expelled French troops (Operation Sabre); now aligned with Russia/Wagner Group; fighting jihadist insurgency (JNIM/ISGS) since 2015; Volunteers for Defense of the Fatherland (VDP) militia; left ECOWAS 2024

infrastructure.notes: Landlocked — fibre via Côte d'Ivoire; Ouaga-Pouga road; Sitarail railway (to Abidjan); Thomas Sankara airport renamed 2022; poor rural road network.

climate_environment.notes: Sahel desertification advancing; Great Green Wall planting; Arly-Singou-Pama wildlife reserves threatened by conflict; gold mining mercury contamination; wood/charcoal deforestation.

debt_aid.notes: Heavily aid-dependent; junta's pivot to Russia complicated Western aid flows; HIPC debt relief beneficiary; cotton subsidies by rich countries harm Burkinabè farmers

top_universities: University of Ouagadougou (now Joseph Ki-Zerbo University)
education.notes: Low literacy (46%); Thomas Sankara's literacy campaigns (1983-87) achieved significant gains; jihadist attacks closing schools in north; French-language instruction; significant gender gap

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 1.5 million (Côte d'Ivoire primary, also Italy, France)
diaspora_migration.notes: Massive seasonal/permanent migration to Côte d'Ivoire (cocoa/coffee plantations); 2002 Ivorian crisis displaced hundreds of thousands of Burkinabè; internally displaced ~2M due to jihadist insurgency

digital_economy.notes: Limited digital infrastructure; FESPACO (Pan-African Film Festival) showcases creative digital economy; mobile money primary financial inclusion tool; conflict disrupting connectivity in north

country_profile.notes_unique: Formerly Upper Volta, renamed by Thomas Sankara (the 'African Che Guevara') who led revolutionary social programmes before his 1987 assassination.
country_profile.national_anthem: Une Seule Nuit (A Single Night — renamed: Ditanyè/Victory Song)

geography.terrain: Gently undulating peneplain; flat savanna; semi-arid north; sandstone escarpment (Banfora Cliffs)
geography.notes: Landlocked in West Africa; Volta River system headwaters; 'Land of the Upright People' (Thomas Sankara's naming); Sahel transition zone; climate change hotspot.

economy_extended.notes: Cotton and gold main exports; rapidly growing gold mining sector (4th in Africa); post-coup economic uncertainty; sanctions; CFA franc zone; 80% rural subsistence farming.

health.notes: Meningitis belt (seasonal epidemics); severe health worker shortage; WHO prequalified malaria vaccine rollout; traditional medicine deeply rooted; free healthcare for under-5s and pregnant women.

food_agriculture.notes: Shea nut processing (women's cooperatives) for cosmetics export; cotton 'white gold'; Bagré growth pole (irrigated agriculture); food insecurity worsening due to jihadist displacement.

energy.notes: Imports electricity from Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana; Zagtouli solar plant (33MW, largest in West Africa at commissioning); Samendéni dam; biomass/charcoal dominant for cooking; severe rural energy poverty.

transport.notes: Landlocked — relies on Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire) and Lomé (Togo) ports; Sitarail railway to Abidjan; extensive unpaved road network; motorcycle dominant rural transport.

tourism.notes: FESPACO (Pan-African Film Festival, biennial, Ouagadougou) — Africa's largest film festival; tourism devastated by security crisis; cultural tourism previously strong; artisan crafts (bronze, textiles).

human_rights_gender.notes: Military junta since 2022 (Capt. Traoré); FGM prevalence high despite laws; child marriage widespread; Sankara-era women's rights legacy eroding; press restrictions post-coup.

active_conflicts: Jihadist insurgency (JNIM, ISGS — controls ~40% of territory)
security_stability.notes: One of world's fastest-growing crises; JNIM/ISGS control swathes of north/east; 2M+ displaced; French military expelled (2022); Russian Wagner/Africa Corps presence; VDP (Volunteers for Defence of the Fatherland) auxiliary militia; AES alliance with Mali/Niger.

cultural_heritage.film_industry: Major (FESPACO host — Ouagadougou is 'Hollywood of Africa')
intangible_heritage_items: Coat of arms ceremony of the Moogho Naaba
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: RTB state broadcaster; private radio active (Radio Omega, Savane FM); press freedom restricted post-coup; community radio vital in rural areas
cultural_heritage.notes: Thomas Sankara (1983-87) revolutionary leader (Pan-Africanist icon); FESPACO world-renowned; Mossi Kingdom (Moro-Naba) cultural continuity; artisan traditions (bronze casting, weaving).

legal_system.sharia_applicability: None (some informal Islamic dispute resolution in north)
legal_system.customary_law_role: Significant in rural areas (land, family disputes)
legal_system.notes: Constitution suspended after 2022 coup; transition charter in place; ASCE-LC (anti-corruption authority); Transitional Legislative Assembly; justice system strained by conflict.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: FESPACO host; Sahel security crisis epicentre; major gold producer; Thomas Sankara legacy.
